A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their main text and Appendices A–H are readable, and figures, tables, and experimental content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendices F–H report original model-response experiments, correlations, and persona disparities across four evaluation datasets.

after.justification: The original empirical results remain, with additional numerical reporting of pairwise persona differences in Tables 5–7.

M1.justification: The six persona-cue procedures, demographic controls, and response-generation approach remain unchanged. Presenting the setup as a flexible benchmark and renaming the name-based non-binary condition to unisex do not establish procedural changes.

E1.justification: Both use SBB and its five domains, MMMD, AITA, and IssueBench, with the same demographic coverage and PRISM, ImplicitPersona, and voter-registration sources. The unisex relabeling retains the existing name-selection population.

E2.justification: The same six cue conditions and no-persona baseline are evaluated across the same seven models. Newly cited studies do not participate as experimental comparators.

E3.justification: Both retain 1,666 evaluation questions, five indicators per persona-cue combination, temperature 1.0, the same preprocessing and controls, and the same outcome metrics. Llama-3.3-70B remains the IssueBench judge; the detailed model descriptions move to Appendix C.

E4.justification: The persona-, model-, and task-specific correlation analyses and ANOVA/Tukey-Kramer comparisons are retained. Tables 5–7 provide detailed outputs of those existing comparisons; no distinct ablation, robustness test, or case study is added.

E5.justification: Three sampled responses, 1,000 bootstrap resamples, confidence intervals, and statistical tests remain unchanged. However, new Tables 5–6 label significance as 0.01%, conflicting with alpha = 0.01 in the methods, Appendix H, and Table 7. This introduces a reporting inconsistency without establishing a changed testing procedure.

E6.justification: Section 4 corrects the invalid-response percentage from 0.57% to 0.98%, matching Appendix D in both versions. Tables 5–7 newly report exact pairwise differences, including a 0.071 AITA accuracy difference between male and non-binary personas under explicit-user cues. Main trends remain stable, although the new 'up to 5,000$' salary summary understates the 7,848.817 difference reported in Table 6.

T1.justification: No formal theory, proofs, or new mathematical definitions are introduced. Adding 'for the same persona' to the correlation null hypothesis clarifies the existing comparison.

C1.justification: The introduction and conclusion newly identify a flexible, reusable benchmark as an explicit contribution, and the recommendation now also addresses engineers testing models before deployment. The central claims about correlated cues producing different bias findings remain.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 adds explanations involving prompt position and internal demographic representations, without direct mechanism tests. The limitations newly discuss legitimate demographic differences in medical advice, while Appendix A.1 expands the qualification of unisex names as a proxy. Appendix H adds a warning against comparing effect sizes across datasets.

D1.justification: Prompt templates, demographic controls, preprocessing, model identifiers, hardware, runtimes, judge instructions, and repository access remain substantively unchanged. V2 relocates model details and adds reasons for existing choices, including the budget-based selection of GPT-4o-mini.

R1.justification: V2 adds discussion of Neumann et al. (2025), concurrent Tonneau et al. (2026), and several supporting studies. It explicitly acknowledges conflicting findings about system versus user prompts. Publication updates and deduplicated Gautam and Wang references retain the same underlying works.

P1.justification: V2 adds a contribution paragraph and discussion, reorganizes limitations under topical headings, moves detailed model descriptions into Appendix C, and edits terminology, affiliations, and prose. The overall section sequence and narrative remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is systematically revised: heatmaps are recolored and reordered, outcome plots receive aligned scales and revised markers, legends, and baseline displays, and the setup diagram is updated. V1 Figure 13 becomes main-text Figure 5; v1 Figures 5–7 become appendix Figure 11. Three new numerical tables are added.

improvement.justification: V2 offers a limited gain in transparency through exact pairwise reporting, clearer treatment of the unisex-name proxy, and correction of the invalid-response summary. These benefits are constrained by inconsistent significance captions, the inaccurate salary summary, and added mechanism explanations without direct tests. The underlying empirical support remains substantially unchanged.
